free_tier.stated: The Hobby plan is free with all platform features: 8 hours of compute time a month, 3 million function requests a month, 1 TB a month of data transfer, 10 workloads and 1 workspace, with no card. Each invocation is capped at 512 MB of isolate memory, 2 s of CPU time, 5 minutes of wall clock, 50 sub-requests and a 100 MB body.

egress.terms: Hobby includes 1 TB a month of data transfer; Hobby has no overage price, and usage above the limits may need an upgrade or restrict the account. Pro and Enterprise bill beyond the included amount at on-demand prices.
egress.price_per_tb: Hobby: no overage price published. Pro and Enterprise on-demand: USD 0.085 per GB in the United States for the next 9 TB after the first 1 TB, i.e. USD 85 per TB (USD 0.11 per GB in Brazil, USD 0.198 per GB in Latam and other regions)

interface_detail: CLI, API, GraphQL API and Terraform, per the Azion pricing page: "CLI, API, GraphQL API, Terraform"
tooling: the azion CLI, per the Azion CLI page: "puts the Azion Platform behind one terminal command, `azion`"
chaining: 8 compute-hours plus 1 TB of egress a month is the largest free egress allowance found, so the shape that fits is a mostly-cached site with a thin function edge; the 2 s CPU ceiling per call forces the heavy work off the edge.

limits.value: 8 compute-hours a month is the wall, not the 3 million requests: at the 2 s per-invocation CPU ceiling that is 14,400 maximum-length invocations before the allowance is gone, while the request counter would still read 0.5 percent used.
